title: Taverna bill: myths vs facts

slides.headline: Your Greek taverna bill, decoded
slides.line: Four things visitors get wrong about eating out in Greece.

slides.headline: "The bread is free"
slides.line: Bread often arrives without asking, and it is usually charged. Say if you do not want it.

slides.headline: Fish is priced by the kilo
slides.line: The menu price is per kilo, not per plate. Ask the weight and price before cooking.

slides.headline: "You must tip 15%"
slides.line: Tipping is optional. About 5–10% in cash if you were happy.

slides.headline: Kerasméno means on the house
slides.line: That dessert you did not order? A gift from the taverna. Say efcharistó.

slides.headline: You should get a receipt
slides.line: And you can pay by card: restaurants must have a card terminal.

slides.headline: Order several dishes and share
slides.line: Plates go in the middle and everyone helps themselves. Order more later.

slides.line: A flat rate on foreign income for retirees who move. Here are the numbers.

slides.line: Not just the pension: all foreign-source income, at one flat rate.

title: AMKA: myths vs facts

slides.headline: The AMKA, explained
slides.line: Greece's social security number, without the confusion.

slides.headline: "The AMKA is your tax number"
slides.line: No. The tax number is the AFM. The AMKA is social security.

slides.headline: You apply in person
slides.line: At a KEP citizens' centre or a branch of e-EFKA.

slides.headline: EU citizens bring ID
slides.line: A passport or national ID card. Take your AFM and proof of address too.

slides.headline: Non-EU needs a work-access permit
slides.line: The official site lists a permit giving access to the labour market.

slides.headline: "Every permit holder gets one"
slides.line: Financially Independent Person permit holders generally cannot, and keep private insurance.

slides.headline: "AMKA means free healthcare"
slides.line: Cover depends on insurance: work, or a registered S1 form.

slides.line: Apply online or in person; it is posted to you.
